answer: Contribution Decay Prism. Each identity earns rewards through a prism that splits payouts across many independent tasks, and only the lowest-performing slice sets your effective rate. To gain full weight, an attacker must sustain that minimum across every slice, which costs real compute and coordination per identity. A terrace of marginal tasks gradually lowers returns as identity count grows, so mass registration yields diminishing payouts. The anchor is a rolling reputation window: new identities start at the floor and need continuous, distinct work to climb,
